fields.label: State
fields.description: Resolved is terminal. A recurrence after resolution opens a NEW row rather than reopening this one — reopening would overwrite the resolution timestamp and destroy the only evidence that the problem is flapping rather than continuing.

fields.label: Subsystem
fields.description: One of chat.governance.alert_rules.SUBSYSTEMS. Enumerated rather than free text because the deduplication key is built from it, and 'relay' / 'Relay' / 'relay_worker' would be three incidents.

fields.label: Scope
fields.description: The object the problem is about — a room, a chain, a space. Two rooms with stuck queues are two incidents; one room reporting hourly is one.

fields.label: Deduplication Key
fields.description: subsystem::kind::scope. Deliberately NOT unique: a resolved incident that recurs must be able to open a second row with the same key, and a unique index would make the recurrence fail to insert instead.

fields.label: Notifications Sent
fields.description: Occurrences 1, 2, 4, 8, 16… notify; the rest update this row silently. Thirty-two occurrences page six times rather than thirty-two, and the gaps widen as the incident ages rather than stopping.

fields.label: Detail
fields.description: The measured values, which is why they are here and never in the deduplication key. Overwritten by the newest occurrence: the current numbers are what an operator needs, and the history of the numbers is what the counters are for.

fields.label: Transports
fields.description: Channels this alert was allowed to use. Subsystems that carry their own delivery never use the operations space — an alert about the relay would join the queue it is reporting on.

fields.label: Undeliverable
fields.description: Set when this alert reached nothing but the log. A configuration gap that silences alerting is the one gap that cannot report itself, so it is recorded here rather than inferred from an absence.

fields.label: Resolution Note
fields.description: Written by the clearing check, not by a human: an alert that the system can see is fixed says so itself, so the board shows what is wrong now rather than everything that was ever wrong.
